deltas.delta: Nethermind 2.3.0-rc (pre-release, tag 2.3.0-rc, published 2026-11-23) pins Nethermind.Numerics.Int256 1.15.0; the current release 2.2.2 pins 1.11.0. Between the two, 24 routines of UInt256.divmod.cs changed (Divide, Mod, DivideFull, ModFull, MultiplyModWideCore, Remainder512By256Bits, Remainder512By192Bits, the reciprocal routines, the power of two divide and mod helpers, the 64, 128 and 192 bit dividers), three were added (QuotientBy64BitsX86Base, URem2By1, Remainder256ByTopLimb254), and a new file UInt256.barrett.cs routes MULMOD by a modulus whose top limb matches BN254 r or p, secp256k1 n, P-256 p or n or the Stark prime through Barrett reduction, and by any modulus 2^256 - c with c below 2^64 - 1 through a pseudo-Mersenne fold, when the high half of the product is at least 2^128. Release dates on NuGet: 1.12.0 2026-10-20, 1.13.0 2026-11-12, 1.14.0 2026-11-13, 1.15.0 2026-11-16.

Nethermind 2.3.0-rc interpreter changes on the paths the PoolManager uses: SDIV and SMOD now call SignedDivide256 and SignedMod256, which wrap Int256.Divide and Int256.Mod as before; MULMOD and ADDMOD read their first two operands in place in the stack and write the result into the modulus slot after copying the modulus to a local; EXP gains a power of two shortcut. The jump destination analyser file is byte identical to 2.2.2. Untraced execution fuses PUSH2 followed by JUMP or JUMPI (and CALLSUB when enabled), skipping the pushed word and the landed JUMPDEST, while traced execution runs the instructions one by one. The PoolManager build has 709 PUSH2 then JUMP or JUMPI pairs.

findings.title: Nethermind's next release pins an integer library eleven days old that rewrites division and remainder and adds Barrett reduction to MULMOD, and no public endpoint lets anyone test a Nethermind node
findings.difference: Ethereum validators run five execution clients with their own 256 bit arithmetic. Nethermind, which reports 25 to 43 percent of validators, publishes 2.3.0-rc on 2026-11-23 with Nethermind.Numerics.Int256 1.15.0 (published 2026-11-16), against 1.11.0 in the current release 2.2.2. The new version changes 24 division and remainder routines, adds three, and adds Barrett reduction for six named moduli and a pseudo-Mersenne fold for moduli 2^256 - c with c below 2^64 - 1. One added test in Remainder512By256Bits and Remainder512By192Bits drops the leading quotient digit when the dividend's top limb is below the divisor's top limb, which is the kind of shortcut that broke ruint 1.21.0. No public Ethereum endpoint names Nethermind, so none of the 200,127 vectors or the script sets has run on it.
findings.mechanism: Every swap and liquidity change reaches MULMOD through FullMath. mulDiv computes mulmod(a, b, 2^256 - 1) first (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24); Nethermind sends that modulus to a fold of the high half into the low half, present unchanged since 1.11.0, before any Barrett or pseudo-Mersenne test. The remainder mulmod(a, b, denominator) at FullMath.sol:48 and :112 and at SqrtPriceMath.sol:252 can reach the new reductions only when a times b is at least 2^384. Read against the callers, that never happens: Position.sol:94-96 multiplies a 256 bit fee growth by a 128 bit liquidity, SqrtPriceMath.sol:47, :71 and :208-209 multiply a liquidity shifted by 96 (below 2^224) by a price below 2^160, SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105 multiply an amount by 2^96, and SwapMath.sol:65, :74 and :104 multiply by at most 10^6. The 4 limb remainder routine is reached at SqrtPriceMath.sol:44-47, where the denominator numerator1 + amount x price can be any value up to 2^256 - 1. Its new leading digit test is correct: with N the dividend, d the divisor and m = uLen - 4, the leading digit is zero exactly when floor(N / b^m) < d, and a top limb below d3 implies that, before or after normalisation. A Python transcription of that routine in both the hardware division arm and the reciprocal arm gave the exact remainder for 489,674 cases, 73,660 of them shaped as SqrtPriceMath.sol:44-47, and a planted <= in place of < gave 586 mismatches. The reciprocal, 64 bit, pseudo-Mersenne, all ones fold, signed remainder, limb negation and power of two exponent routines gave no mismatch on 2,914,162 cases, and six planted faults were caught. A wrong result on a Nethermind node would make it compute a different post-state for a block that contains the swap. The client cannot steal: geth and the other clients hold the majority, so the Nethermind nodes would reject canonical blocks or propose blocks the rest reject. If more than one third of validators ran the faulty build, finality would stall until it was fixed.
findings.impact: No loss of pool funds. A fault would cost Nethermind validators missed duties and could delay finality; balances on the canonical chain follow the clients that compute the specified result.
findings.preconditions: A fault in a Nethermind Int256 routine that this transcription does not cover (Remainder512By192Bits, MulModBy128Bits, the 128 and 192 bit dividers, the .NET JIT output) and validators that upgrade to 2.3.0 with that fault. An ordinary account cannot choose which client builds or validates its block.
findings.mitigations: Nothing for the deployer or LPs on Ethereum. Node operators who use Nethermind can stay on 2.2.2 until 2.3.0 final has run the consensus test suites; the review can rerun the transcriptions on the version 2.3.0 final pins.

cleared.check: Whether the new Barrett and pseudo-Mersenne paths of Int256 1.15.0 can be reached from any MULMOD in src.
cleared.result: They run only when the high half of the product is at least 2^128 and the modulus has four limbs with a matching top limb (UInt256.std.cs:399-412). The only MULMOD whose product can exceed 2^384 is FullMath.sol:24, whose modulus 2^256 - 1 takes the fold in MultiplyModWideCore first. Every other MULMOD (FullMath.sol:48 and :112 through each caller, SqrtPriceMath.sol:252) multiplies operands whose product is below 2^384, as listed in the finding. A pool cannot steer a MULMOD into these paths.

cleared.check: The leading quotient digit test that Int256 1.15.0 added to Remainder512By256Bits and Remainder512By192Bits, the 4 limb remainder MULMOD reaches at SqrtPriceMath.sol:44-47.
cleared.result: Correct by argument and by test. The leading digit of the normalised division is zero exactly when floor(N / b^(uLen - 4)) < d; a top dividend limb below d3 gives that, and it also keeps the extra limb zero because d3 < 2^(64 - shift). The test is strict, unlike the <= of ruint 1.21.0. The transcription in scripts/neth_rem512.py, both arms, gave the exact remainder on 489,674 cases, 83,280 with the top limb at d3 - 1, d3 or d3 + 1, and without the test also on 39,130; the planted <= gave 586 mismatches, all in that edge shape.

cleared.check: Nethermind's fused PUSH2 with JUMP or JUMPI in untraced execution, against the unfused sequence, at 2.2.2 and 2.3.0-rc.
cleared.result: Same stack, gas, program counter and outcome as read. The fused path decodes the two byte destination big endian, charges 3, then 8 or 10, then 1 for the landed JUMPDEST, pops only the condition for JUMPI and tests all 32 bytes, validates the destination only when the jump is taken, and keeps the stack limit at 1,024 (MaxStackSize is 1,025 and the prelude rejects a head of 1,024 or more). Code is padded, so a truncated PUSH2 at the end reads zeros and is followed by STOP. Its only effect is that a trace runs the other path.

cleared.result: It executes neither. A linear decode of research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json finds one 0x0a and one 0x08 at instruction boundaries, at pcs 24008 and 24005, after the INVALID at 23996, inside the solc metadata that encodes version 0.8.26. src has no exponent operator and no addmod.

cleared.check: Besu's arithmetic handlers for the opcodes the pool math depends on.
cleared.result: MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, MOD, SDIV and SMOD use java.math.BigInteger at 26.11.0 and on main. SDIV of -2^255 by -1 gives 2^255, whose 33 byte encoding is cut to the low 32 bytes, which is -2^255 as specified. SMOD keeps the sign of the dividend. SAR returns the sign fill for counts of 2^31 or more and for counts above four bytes.

cleared.check: EIP-8024 jump destination rule in the clients that ship it for Glamsterdam (part of lead L-1216 for Ethereum).
cleared.result: EIP-8024 keeps jump destination analysis unchanged. geth master core/vm/analysis_legacy.go is byte identical to v1.17.10 and masks only PUSH immediates. Nethermind 2.3.0-rc adds DUPN, SWAPN and EXCHANGE as handlers and its JumpDestinationAnalyzer.cs is byte identical to 2.2.2. Cycle 29 read evm2 e80df9c4's analysis as identical to 66687c18. The PoolManager has no 0xe6 to 0xe8 at an instruction boundary, so no jump destination of it moves.

cleared.check: Glamsterdam assumed live in January 2027 with EIP-8037 as written and EIP-8038: can its gas rules make a withdrawal, a swap or a settlement impossible, or change what a PoolManager call returns?
cleared.result: No. src never branches on gas: payouts and hook calls pass gas() (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134), and under EIP-8037 the state gas reservoir passes whole to the child while gas() returns the execution gas left. modifyLiquidity writes a fixed set of slots (two ticks, up to two bitmap words, one position, the pool liquidity), about nine new slots for a fresh range, which costs about 0.9 million state gas outside the 16,777,216 execution cap and about 0.1 million execution gas for writes. A swap that crosses an initialized tick pays two STORAGE_WRITE of 10,000 instead of 2,800 for the fee growth outside words; by my estimate one transaction still crosses several hundred initialized ticks, and a longer swap can be split by price limit. A native take to a new account pays 183,600 state gas, which the caller's transaction pays. None of this moves value. ETH transfer logs (EIP-7708), the SELFDESTRUCT burn removal (EIP-8246) and the factory predeploy (EIP-7997) touch no PoolManager balance.

leads.question: Is there any public Ethereum endpoint that names Nethermind or Besu in web3_clientVersion and accepts eth_call with state overrides, so the battery and script sets can run on a non-reth, non-geth, non-erigon interpreter?
leads.why: Every live run on Ethereum so far reached reth, geth and erigon only; 43 endpoints were tried this cycle.

leadResults.answer: No attribution method exists yet. Pocket still routes each batch element to its own backend: 30 three-element bracket batches came back from 19 different combinations of seven builds. The reth v2.10.1 and v2.11.0 interpreters compute the same result for every input as read in cycle 27, so no in-EVM probe can separate them. The run was repeated: all 200,127 vectors with four sends per batch, 1,336 sends, 0 mismatches. reth v2.10.1 named itself in 1,198 of 2,672 bracket reads (44.8 percent), so with independent routing each batch reached it at least once with probability about 91 percent. The 'pinned to v2.10.1' results of cycles 24, 26 and 27 stay unpinned.

erigon 3.8.2 (go1.27.2 and go1.27.4 builds) named itself in 126 of 2,672 Pocket bracket reads (4.7 percent). The four-send rerun of all 200,127 vectors found no mismatch from any backend, which reaches erigon 3.8.2 for about 18 percent of batches. No request is shown to have run on it, and sequences c and c2 were not rerun this cycle.

For Ethereum: EIP-8024 keeps jump destination analysis unchanged, geth master's analysis file equals v1.17.10, Nethermind 2.3.0-rc's analyser equals 2.2.2, and the PoolManager has no 0xe6 to 0xe8 at an instruction boundary. On the gas edges: src passes gas() to every call and never reads gas otherwise, and under EIP-8037 gas() returns the execution gas left while the state reservoir passes whole to the child, so a client fault in EIP-8037 or EIP-8038 accounting would change gas used or an out of gas outcome, which is a consensus fault of that client, not a different PoolManager result on the canonical chain. Glamsterdam is set for Hoodi on 2026-12-15 and has no mainnet date. The ArbOS and OP Stack parts of the lead belong to their units.

No reth release pins evm2 e80df9c4 yet. reth main still reads version 2.11.0 with that pin (Cargo.toml lines 2 and 451-454), and the tags v2.11.1, v2.12.0 and v2.12.0-rc.1 do not exist. Every reth endpoint seen names v2.11.0 or older. The lead waits for the release.

No endpoint that serves only erigon 3.8.2 was found. 25 endpoints in the main survey and 18 more were queried; none named erigon except the Pocket gateway, which mixes erigon 3.8.2 with six other builds. Erigon tag v3.8.3 does not exist, so 3.8.2 is still the newest release.
